name: Front terrace

dimensions.notes: Scaled from the 1:50 survey — approx. ±10 cm. Ceiling height as surveyed.

orientation: Street-facing, full width of the façade, balustrade with two piers

photos.caption: Looking along the terrace: lounge doors open, gas barbecue, antenna mast
Mountain end: bistro chairs, orange downpipe, view to the mountains
The front double doors from outside — painted green, reflecting the village

current.summary: Long, narrow terrace (≈6.1 × 1.35 m) across the top of the façade, reached through the lounge's front double doors — which are painted a deep green outside. Red quarry-tile floor, iron railings between rendered masonry piers. One end has a gas barbecue, a folding table and the TV antenna mast; the other end looks straight at the mountains, with two bistro chairs. The house wall is weathered render with mould staining and patches, a new dark metal gutter at the eaves and an orange PVC downpipe.
keep: The views: village, church and the mountain
issues: Weathered render with mould staining — clean, repair, mineral/lime paint
Bright orange PVC downpipe — paint to match the wall or replace
Antenna mast in the middle of the view — move or replace
Door bottom rails weathered; check draught seal
Barbecue here and on the back terrace — decide which terrace is for cooking

target.concept: DRAFT — the view terrace. Keep it simple and narrow-friendly: a slim bench or two bistro chairs and a small round table at the mountain end for morning coffee and sunset drinks, a row of terracotta pots (geraniums, herbs, a small olive) along the railing base, the wall cleaned and painted warm white, and the downpipe and antenna dealt with so nothing interrupts the view.
target.renderPrompt: Photorealistic interior photograph, same camera angle, same room geometry, same windows, doors, beams and walls — do not move or invent architecture. Remove ALL clutter: boxes, tools, clothes, bags, bottles, cables, packaging. Restyle as a narrow Sicilian view terrace. Keep the red quarry-tile floor, the iron railings between rendered piers, the deep-green painted glazed double doors and the mountain view. Walls cleaned and painted warm white, no mould or patches; the downpipe painted to match the wall; no TV antenna. A small round black iron bistro table with two folding chairs at the mountain end, a row of terracotta pots with red geraniums, herbs and a small olive tree along the base of the railing. Morning light, no people.
